turns.prompt_text: I have a 20 gallon fish tank
turns.response_html:
That's a great starter size! It offers enough water volume to stay stable while fitting in most rooms.

Are you planning on a community tank with small fish like tetras, or a single-species setup?

turns.prompt_text: I would like to add multiple species
turns.response_html:
A 20-gallon tank is often considered the "sweet spot" for a community setup—it’s large enough to house a variety of personalities but small enough to manage easily.

Since you're looking for multiple species, here are three distinct "vibes" based on different aquatic communities:

1. The Classic Colorful Community

This setup focuses on high activity and bright colors.

  • Schooling: 6–8 Neon or Cardinal Tetras (electric blue/red).
  • Top Dweller: 1 Honey Gourami (peaceful, yellow/orange center-piece).
  • Bottom Cleaners: 6 Pygmy Corydoras (tiny, energetic catfish).
  • The Utility: 1 Neritina Snail (excellent for algae control).

2. The "Nano" Jungle

If you plan on having lots of live plants, these smaller species will make the tank feel massive.

  • Schooling: 8–10 Chili Rasboras (tiny, deep red).
  • Accent: 6 Endler’s Livebearers (metallic patterns, very active).
  • Invertebrates: A colony of Cherry Shrimp (red, yellow, or blue).
  • Bottom: 3 Otocinclus Catfish (specialized algae eaters).

3. The Hardy & Robust Mix

Great if you want fish that are a bit more forgiving and have "dog-like" personalities.

  • Schooling: 6 White Cloud Mountain Minnows (very hardy, cool fin displays).
  • Mid-Level: 5 Platies (come in almost every color; very curious).
  • Bottom: 1 Bristlenose Pleco (stays small enough for a 20g and looks like a prehistoric dragon).

Three Tips for Success:

  1. The Rule of Three: Try to pick one species for the top, one for the middle, and one for the bottom. This prevents crowding and makes the tank look full.
  2. Bio-Load: Add fish gradually (3–4 at a time) over several weeks. Adding everyone at once can spike the ammonia and crash your cycle.
  3. Plants vs. Plastic: Live plants like Anubias or Java Fern are nearly impossible to kill and help keep the water clean by absorbing nitrates.

Are you leaning toward a specific color palette, or would you like to see a list of local fish stores in the Ames/Ankeny area to go see these in person?
